newsitem.title: MEXICO: Lethal cocktail of drugs killed Mexican kingpin.
newsitem.headline: Lethal cocktail of drugs killed Mexican kingpin.

text.p: A lethal coctail of drugs killed Mexican cocaine baron Amado Carrillo Fuentes, suggesting he died either through medical mishap or foul play, officials said on Friday.

Tests on Carrillo's vital organs showed the kingpin died of respiratory failure from a deadly combination of drugs shortly after he underwent massive plastic surgery to change his appearance, the Attorney General's Office (PGR) said.

Some of the drugs were anaesthetics injected for the operation, but another drug, the depressant Midasolam, was administered after the surgery at a Mexico City hospital and caused his lungs to collapse, the PGR said in a statement.

"The PGR continues its investigations to determine if the injection of this medication (Dormicum), which caused the death of Amado Carrillo Fuentes, was done on purpose or was an ill-advised mistake by medics in charge of the patient," it said.
The news raised fresh questions over whether a rival drugs gang or someone within his own Juarez Cartel may have caused the July 4 death of Carrillo Fuentes, 42, and Mexico's most wanted drug lord.
Mexican network Televisa reported two weeks ago that it was told by an unidentified source at the hospital that one of Carrillo's bodyguards must have murdered him.

The tale of the cocaine capo's untimely death has unfolded in a bizarre fashion. Officials were unsure if a corpse that had been flown to northern Mexico and back to the capital was that of the drug trafficker.

His face was so altered by the plastic surgery that authorities had to wait a week for a DNA test to be totally sure they had finally gotten the man they had chased unsuccessfully for nearly nine years.
The medic who operated on Carrillo Fuentes has been reported missing and one newspaper suggested he had been killed or was being held by other cartel members to avoid giving information.
